Are you a fresher looking to break into the tech industry as a Full Stack Developer in 2024?
Do you want to know what skills are essential to stand out and succeed in this dynamic field? You’re in the right place! In this comprehensive guide, we’ll dive deep into the essential skills every aspiring
Full Stack Developer
needs to master to excel in the ever-evolving world of web development.
Introduction
Full Stack Development is one of the most sought-after roles in the tech industry today. As companies continue to shift towards digital platforms, the demand for skilled Full Stack Developers has skyrocketed. But what exactly does it take to become a Full Stack Developer, especially as a fresher in 2024?
The Core Skills Required For Full-Stack Developers
HTML and CSS
HTML (Hypertext Markup Language): The backbone of web pages. It structures content using tags.
CSS (Cascading Style Sheets): Works with HTML to style web pages, controlling colors, fonts, and layouts.
JavaScript
The programming language that makes web pages interactive.
Frameworks: Proficiency in frameworks like React and Angular is essential for creating dynamic user experiences.
Back-End Technologies
Node.js: Allows running JavaScript on the server.
Express.js: A framework for building web applications with Node.js.
Java: Often used for server applications with frameworks like Spring.
Python: Popular for back-end development, especially with frameworks like Django.
Databases
SQL Databases: MySQL and PostgreSQL.
NoSQL Databases: MongoDB for managing and retrieving data effectively.
Version Control
Git: Essential for tracking changes in code and collaborating with other developers.
Platforms: GitHub for managing and maintaining project histories.
Web Hosting Platforms
Amazon Web Services (AWS): For deploying applications online.
Heroku: Simplifies the deployment process for web applications.
Web Architecture
Understanding client-server models, RESTful APIs, and microservices to design scalable and high-performing systems.
Front-End Frameworks
Proficiency in frameworks like AngularJS to build interactive web applications.
Basic Design Skills
Grasping design principles to create user-friendly interfaces.
Creativity
Essential for developing engaging and innovative web solutions.
Strategic Planning
Effective planning for the design, development, and implementation phases.
Analytical Skills
Analyzing information to make data-driven decisions.
Problem-Solving Skills
Addressing and resolving development challenges efficiently.
Time Management
Prioritizing tasks to meet deadlines and produce quality work.
Communication Skills
Explaining technical concepts clearly to team members and stakeholders.
Attention to Detail
Ensuring code accuracy and high quality through careful testing and review.
Programming Languages
Familiarity with multiple programming languages, including JavaScript, Python, Ruby, and Java.
Soft Skills
Teamwork, adaptability, and effective communication for successful collaboration.
APIs
Understanding how to create and manage APIs for building functional applications.
Spring Framework
For those working with Java, knowledge of the Spring Framework simplifies application development.
In-Depth Look At Essential Full Stack Developer Skills 2024
Mastering HTML and CSS
HTML and CSS are the building blocks of web development. Freshers must understand the basics of HTML5, including semantic tags, forms, and multimedia elements. CSS3 skills should encompass layout techniques (Flexbox, Grid), animations, and responsive design principles.
JavaScript and Its Ecosystem
JavaScript remains a critical skill for Full Stack Developers. Freshers should not only learn vanilla JavaScript but also get comfortable with ES6+ features. Mastering popular JavaScript frameworks like React and Angular is crucial, as they are widely used in the industry.
Diving into Back-End Technologies
Back-end development involves creating and managing server-side logic. Freshers should focus on Node.js and Express.js for JavaScript-based back-end development. Additionally, understanding other languages like Python (with Django) and Java (with Spring) will provide a competitive edge.
Database Management
A comprehensive understanding of
both SQL (MySQL, PostgreSQL) and NoSQL (MongoDB) databases is essential.
Freshers should learn how to design, implement, and manage databases, ensuring efficient data storage and retrieval.
Version Control with Git
Git is an indispensable tool for modern developers. Freshers must learn how to use Git for version control, including creating repositories, committing changes, branching, and merging. Familiarity with GitHub for collaboration is also vital.
Deploying with Web Hosting Platforms
Knowing how to deploy applications is critical. Freshers should get hands-on experience with platforms like AWS and Heroku. Understanding cloud services, server management, and deployment pipelines will make them more versatile developers.
Understanding Web Architecture
A solid grasp of web architecture principles, including client-server models, RESTful services, and microservices, is necessary. This knowledge helps in designing scalable, efficient, and maintainable applications.

Job Title: Forward Deployed Engineer (Pre & Post Sale)
Location: Mountain View, CA or New York, NY (Office-based)
Duration: Long Term
Client: Direct
Travel: Up to 70% (Customer Sites)
About the Role
Enterprise Suite is how the world's fastest-growing mid-market and enterprise finance teams run their books, close their quarter, and put AI agents to work on real accounting operations. Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) are the team that makes that real: embedded with our customers, shipping production automation, and turning "AI pilot" into "AI in the general ledger." This isn't a traditional sales engineering role, and it isn't a traditional product engineering role either. FDEs report into Engineering, work shoulder-to-shoulder with Sales and Account Management on the deals and renewals that matter most, and own the last mile between what Core Engineering ships and what a specific customer actually runs. You'll sit at the intersection of engineering, applied AI, and enterprise finance.
Responsibilities
What you'll do
Pre-sale: Build the proof that wins the deal
Get hands-on with prospects before there's a contract: build a working proof-of-value directly in (or against a realistic replica of) the prospect's own data and systems — real integrations and real output, not a scripted demo.
Partner with Account Executives from first technical touch: run discovery with the prospect's finance and IT teams to understand their chart of accounts, systems, and process gaps well enough to build against them.
Lead the technical evaluation: architecture and security/compliance reviews, integration feasibility, and technical RFP responses with the prospect's IT and controllership teams.
Build the technical narrative and ROI case alongside Sales and present it directly to economic buyers — CFOs and Controllers — as part of the deal cycle. Your proof-of-value is very often what gets the deal signed.
Flag technical or data-readiness risk early, so Sales scopes and prices the deal accurately and nothing you built pre-sale becomes a surprise post-signature.
Post-sale: Architect and ship in customer-specific production
Architect and deploy customer-specific configurations of AI Agents that automate complex accounting processes — strengthening internal controls, closing books faster, and removing manual work from real customer environments.
Perform deep technical troubleshooting: review and edit Python, write SQL for integrations, and diagnose configuration issues across customer systems.
Serve as the functional and technical escalation point for issues involving integrations, data flows, and automation logic — including reviewing and optimizing SQL-based validations and API-driven workflows.
Maintain SLAs for response and resolution; document issues comprehensively and escalate to Engineering with complete context.
Post-sale: Own the customer relationship and drive expansion
Lead high-impact transformation engagements with enterprise finance teams — diagnosing operational bottlenecks and identifying where AI Agents create the most leverage.
Act as the primary technical point of contact across implementations, engaging directly with CFOs, Controllers, and accounting leaders.
Guide and train customer teams through workflow redesign, change management, and the value realization required to scale AI Agent adoption across their organization — and carry that same proof-of-value discipline into expansion and renewal conversations.
Travel to customer sites as needed (up to 70%) for pre-sale technical evaluation, hands-on deployment, training, and adoption workshops.
Ongoing: Shape the product and the playbook
Be the Voice of the Customer: surface technical feedback, integration requirements, and product gaps to Product and Core Engineering — as input to their roadmap, not a substitute for it.
Partner with Product Management on learnings from onsite discovery sessions to design workflows centered on AI Agent deployment and business outcomes.
Build the playbook: create implementation guides, expansion frameworks, and reusable assets so every deployment makes the next one faster.
Educate customers and internal teams on the strategic value of AI-enabled workflow transformation and best practices for building durable AI Agents.
Where this role sits
FDEs report into Engineering, not Sales — but this is very much a field role, spanning both sides of the signature, and the two partnerships below are the job as much as the code is.
Your partnership with Sales & Account Management
You're the technical face of Enterprise Suite in the field, on both sides of the deal: Account Executives pull you in pre-sale to build the proof-of-value that wins the technical evaluation, and Customer Success pulls you in post-sale for QBRs, renewals, and expansion.
Deals and renewals in this business run on proof, not promises — you're the one who produces it, first as a working pilot in the sales cycle, then as a live production system afterward. That makes you directly responsible for de-risking the pipeline, even though you don't carry a number yourself.
You'll work daily with Account Executives and Customer Success on the accounts you're assigned to; you won't be measured on bookings, but expect to be in the room for the technical parts of both the sale and the renewal.

Striveworks is a pioneering organization dedicated to helping clients harness the transformative power of artificial intelligence to address complex national security and business challenges. Founded by a team of experienced data scientists and engineers, the company serves as a central hub that seamlessly integrates data, models, and business outcomes. Its mission is to simplify the journey from AI deployment to continuous optimization, ensuring systems remain reliable, adaptable, and scalable in an unpredictable world. Striveworks specializes in developing mission-critical AI solutions that perform reliably across diverse environments, scale efficiently with increasing workloads, and adapt rapidly to technological advancements. By focusing on increasing system reliability and performance while reducing operational costs, Striveworks empowers organizations to make confident, data-driven decisions in dynamic and high-stakes settings.
About The Role
As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer at Striveworks, you will play a vital role in shaping and leading the company’s AI initiatives. You will be entrusted from day one to contribute technically and serve as a customer-facing leader, guiding projects from conception to delivery. Your primary responsibilities will include designing AI-powered solutions, managing data ingestion and processing pipelines, developing analytics, and deploying models that meet critical operational needs. You will collaborate closely with customers, engineers, and stakeholders to understand their requirements, translate them into technical strategies, and oversee the execution to ensure timely delivery aligned with business value. Your expertise will guide the development of advanced machine learning models across various data types such as images, videos, text, geospatial data, and time series. Additionally, you will be involved in improving internal practices, capturing reusable functionalities, and accelerating the delivery of impactful solutions. This role offers flexibility with a fully remote work environment or a hybrid setup at our Austin, TX office, with travel requirements up to 20% for fieldwork and stakeholder engagement.
Qualifications
Advanced degree in data science, machine learning, computer science, or a related discipline
10+ years of relevant professional experience in AI, data science, or software engineering
Expertise in Python, with proficiency in libraries such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, and scikit-learn
Strong knowledge of systems programming languages like Go, Rust, C++, Java, or Scala
Experience designing and deploying complex algorithms, data structures, and analytics in cloud environments
Proven track record of delivering complex technical solutions in production settings
Familiarity with modern software engineering practices including Agile methodologies, version control, CI/CD, and debugging tools
Leadership experience managing cross-functional teams across remote and on-site locations
Excellent communication skills to articulate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences
Eligibility and willingness to obtain and maintain a US Secret (or higher) security clearance

Engage with customers, engineers, and stakeholders to define clear project requirements that leverage AI capabilities to solve real-world problems
Translate business needs into technical approaches, including system design, scoping, and planning
Lead project teams to ensure timely delivery of solutions that deliver measurable business value, while actively contributing to project execution
Design, orchestrate, and automate complex data pipelines and algorithms within modern architectures such as cloud, event-driven, and microservices environments
Guide the development, training, and deployment of machine learning models across various data modalities including images, videos, text, and geospatial data
Identify insights, opportunities, and challenges, providing feedback to improve practices, develop reusable components, and expand company offerings
Conduct mission-critical fieldwork and interface directly with customers and stakeholders at their operational sites
Contribute to the continuous improvement of platform capabilities and internal processes

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Northrop Grumman Space Systems—Missile Defense Integration offers an excellent opportunity for a
Software Engineer (Algorithm) – TRK (26-334)
to join our team of skilled and diverse professionals. Based in Huntsville, AL, this role is essential to supporting the U.S. President, the Secretary of Defense, and combatant commanders at the strategic, regional, and operational levels.
This position does not provide relocation assistance and requires on-site work with no remote options.
Position Overview
The Command and Control, Battle Management, and Communications (C2BMC) program is a key component of the Missile Defense System. It is a vital operational system that enables the U.S. president, the secretary of defense, and combatant commanders at strategic, regional, and operational levels to systematically plan ballistic missile defense operations, collectively monitor the battle, and dynamically control networked sensors and weapon systems to achieve global and regional mission goals. C2BMC supports layered missile defense capabilities that enable an optimized response to threats across all ranges and flight phases. It serves as a force multiplier by networking, integrating, and synchronizing autonomous sensor and weapon systems and operations, both globally and regionally, to improve performance. C2BMC is essential for all ground and flight tests that verify and demonstrate the current and future capabilities of missile defense systems.
As a member of the Regional Applications Agile Release Train (ART) of the Missile Defense National Team for Command and Control, Battle Management, and Communications (C2BMC) (aka C2BMC NT), this position will help generate software design artifacts, implement Java-based software changes, support design and code reviews, and support software testing and the resolution of issues arising from testing. The candidate will be involved in presenting developed designs. The candidate will actively participate in agile planning and execution using established C2BMC processes.
